cannot_decide: Which path is right: two-view is the reference elsewhere in this project, yet no ground truth for arm amplitude exists here, so this cannot say whether two-view shrinks motion or monocular inflates it. Whether YouTube's remainder is signers, clip cutting (0.57 s per token, against D20's 0.30) or framing. Whether a stored 24 fps is the sources' true rate: the clock check moves with signers too. A channel is not a signer. ASLLRP's path was not compared on the same clips. Carry: the word is defined nowhere in the repository, so 1.44x is neither confirmed nor refuted: on hold-x it needs the right wrist at the row's right_needed_for_1_44.
note: Real signing's wrist differs by signer and by corpus far more than the review's first numbers show one by one. Same clips through both paths: the monocular path reads 18-39% more wrist motion at 3 Hz and 23-37% more spread than two-view on every How2Sign signer, while its raw speed is 0.83-1.11x, so How2Sign's small motion could partly come from how it was lifted. Both stored clocks are 24 fps. After the path is matched, YouTube still reads about 1.5x D20 at both raw and 3 Hz. Composition's excess over real grows when jitter is filtered: top10 1.77x raw, 2.20x at 3 Hz.
